description: Holder of one Dolphin terminal as a Crab worker: host-wide singleton lock, create or adopt a tmux session running the configured command, optional pin of a self-updating CLI, graceful SIGTERM stop, exit when the session or command ends; never sends keys.
state: Exclusive flock held for the holder's lifetime (owner record pid/session/socket), the held command's (pid, starttime), pin recheck clock.
forward: lock busy -> AlreadyRunning(5); pin fails -> Unpinned(6); session exists: one live pane whose pane process or direct child runs the command (basename of argv0, equal arguments, #! interpreter prefix allowed) -> adopted, else Conflict(3) untouched; else new-session -d with command plus rendered prompt argument, owner option. Poll: stop flag -> SIGTERM command, wait grace 1..8 s, kill-session; session gone or command gone -> Ended(0); pin recheck every 60 s, failure -> stop and Unpinned.
inverse: Excluded: a second holder of one lock, keystrokes (send-keys/load-buffer/paste-buffer), touching a conflicting session, starting an unpinned program, an unbound or unused prompt placeholder.
From an exit status one recovers the outcome class only; the owner record names the last holder, not earlier ones.
cost: Per poll: has-session (one tmux client) and one /proc stat read; adoption scans /proc once for direct children (bounded 65536 entries); the pin hashes one file and runs one bounded version command (15 s) per check.
checks: 2026-11-04: 10 tests on private tmux servers (create/stop, session ends, adopt under a shell, conflict untouched, command ends inside a surviving shell, singleton across two tmux servers with an in-test --no-singleton red control, lock release, prompt as argument with a keystroke audit, pin/login refusal, argument refusals); red controls: lock disabled, match always true, send-keys added, pin check removed.
limitations: Cooperative same-user processes; the lock is per lock file, not per session name; real Claude/Copilot TUIs and their idle markers are not exercised; tool restriction flags of a CLI are the deployment's responsibility.
